title: When the Group Chat Sings
premise: Cyrus Ravensworth has survived high school by being unremarkable, channeling everything she can't say into the bread she bakes at her family's shop. But when she's paired with her nemesis, popular and polished Wren Castillo, for a semester-long local history project, they unearth a decades-old cover-up: the school board knowingly let a beloved teacher take the fall for a fire that closed the old vocational wing—and buried evidence that students were hurt. As the board closes ranks and threatens Cyrus's scholarship and her family's bakery lease, Cyrus must choose between the invisibility that kept her safe and the voice the group chat she never meant to join is begging her to use. In the end, Cyrus testifies at the school board meeting, the truth is restored to the record, and she stops baking her feelings into bread—she starts saying them out loud.
about_author: Rosalind Ashgrove grew up above her grandmother's bakery, where every argument ended in proofing dough and every reconciliation smelled like cinnamon. She writes stories about quiet kids who learn that silence is a choice, not a destiny.

chapters.title: The Sourdough Rule
chapters.summary: POV Cyrus. Cyrus introduces her survival system: head down, grades up, locker shut, feelings kneaded into bread. A failed group assignment reminds her why invisibility is safer. Emotional beat: the ache of being perfectly unseen.

chapters.title: Assigned Seating, Assigned Doom
chapters.summary: POV Cyrus. Mr. Okafor pairs Cyrus with Wren Castillo for the semester-long 'Unsung History of Millbrook High' project. Their first meeting in the library is pure venom—until Wren admits she needs this project to salvage her own reputation. Emotional beat: grudging, wary truce.

chapters.title: What the Archive Kept
chapters.summary: POV Cyrus. Digging through the basement archives, they find a scorched yearbook and a 1998 article about the vocational wing fire—naming a teacher, Ms. Ferro, as the cause. But a photo shows students in the wing that night, students the official report says weren't there. Emotional beat: the thrill of a wrong door opening.

chapters.title: The Group Chat
chapters.summary: POV Wren. Wren adds Cyrus to a group chat of misfits—archive kid Dev, Ferro's granddaughter Priya, and Wren's ex-best friend Theo. Cyrus resists, but Priya reveals Ferro took the blame to protect a board member's kid. Emotional beat: found family knocking on a locked door.

chapters.title: Rising
chapters.summary: POV Cyrus. The team verifies the cover-up: the fire was electrical, caused by deferred maintenance the board had ignored. Cyrus bakes a celebration loaf for the chat—her first bread baked for people, not against feelings. Emotional beat: cautious hope, the warmth of belonging.

chapters.title: Punch Down
chapters.summary: POV Wren. The board retaliates: Cyrus's scholarship is 'under review,' and the bakery's lease suddenly has problems. Wren, whose mother sits on the board, is pressured to disavow the project. Emotional beat: the price of survival made literal.

chapters.title: Overproofed
chapters.summary: POV Cyrus. Cyrus cracks—she snaps at Wren, skips the chat, and nearly burns down her family's kitchen trying to knead panic into dough. Her father, who once knew Ms. Ferro, finally tells her what really happened that night. Emotional beat: collapse before courage.

chapters.title: The Leavening
chapters.summary: POV Wren. Wren chooses the group chat over her mother's approval, leaking the board's internal emails to Dev. Theo reconciles with her; Cyrus shows up at the bakery at 5 a.m. to help Wren bake bread for the whole school—each loaf with a page of the buried report tucked inside. Emotional beat: alliance forged in flour and defiance.

chapters.title: When the Group Chat Sings
chapters.summary: POV Cyrus. At the board meeting, Cyrus—terrified, voice shaking—testifies, backed by Priya's grandmother's testimony and the whole group chat standing in matching flour-dusted aprons. The room erupts; the board can't silence them all. Emotional beat: the climax—invisibility abandoned, voice found.

chapters.title: Crumb and Crust
chapters.summary: POV Cyrus. The record is corrected; Ferro's name is cleared, and the vocational wing is renamed for her. Cyrus keeps the group chat, keeps Wren, and bakes a plain, perfect loaf—nothing hidden in it, nothing she can't say. Emotional beat: resolution—identity chosen, family found.
